# ScatterplotLayer

<!-- gen:begin summary -->
<!-- Generated by `npm run generate:op-docs` from noodles-validate/registry.json. The title and the text between gen:begin and gen:end markers are replaced on every run; write anywhere else. -->

Render a scatterplot of points as circles on the map.
<!-- gen:end summary -->

## Syntax

<!-- gen:begin syntax -->
```json
{
  "id": "/scatterplot-layer",
  "type": "ScatterplotLayerOp",
  "position": { "x": 0, "y": 0 },
  "data": { "inputs": {} }
}
```

Expressions and code read its fields as `op('/scatterplot-layer').par.data` (an input) and `op('/scatterplot-layer').out.layer` (an output). Edges name the same fields as handles: `par.data`, `out.layer`.
<!-- gen:end syntax -->

## Remarks

ScatterplotLayer draws one circle per row of `data`. Each input whose name starts with `get` takes either a constant, used for every row, or a per-row function from an [Accessor](./accessor.md) or an operator built on one. `getPosition` defaults to the constant `[0, 0, 0]`, so until you connect a position accessor such as `[d.longitude, d.latitude]`, every circle sits on top of the others in the Gulf of Guinea.

A few defaults differ from deck.gl's own ScatterplotLayer, which matters when you port code or follow the deck.gl docs:

| Prop | Here | deck.gl |
|------|------|---------|
| `radiusUnits` | `"pixels"` | `"meters"` |
| `getRadius` | `20` | `1` |
| `stroked` | `true` | `false` |
| `getLineWidth` | `0` | `1` |

Circles therefore keep their size on screen as you zoom. To size them on the ground, set `radiusUnits` to `"meters"` and give `getRadius` a value in meters. The outline is on but has no width until you set `getLineWidth`. Line width is in meters, deck.gl's default `lineWidthUnits`, which this operator has no input for, so a width of `1` vanishes at city zoom. To draw outlines in pixels, pass the layer through [LayerProps](./layer-props.md) with `lineWidthUnits` in `additionalProps`, as in the example below.

Colors are hex strings, with an optional alpha byte (`#ff8800` or `#ff880080`). The operator converts them to the RGBA arrays deck.gl expects, including the values an accessor returns.

You never set `updateTriggers`. The operator builds them from its accessor inputs, so connecting a new accessor redraws the layer. The deck.gl layer id is the operator's path, such as `/points`.

## Examples

Circles sized in meters with a 1 pixel white outline. LayerProps adds the deck.gl props this operator has no inputs for.

```json
{
  "nodes": [
    { "id": "/points", "type": "ScatterplotLayerOp", "position": { "x": 0, "y": 0 }, "data": { "inputs": { "radiusUnits": "meters", "getRadius": 500, "getFillColor": "#ff8800cc", "getLineColor": "#ffffff", "getLineWidth": 1 } } },
    { "id": "/pixel-outline", "type": "LayerPropsOp", "position": { "x": 300, "y": 0 }, "data": { "inputs": { "additionalProps": { "lineWidthUnits": "pixels" } } } }
  ],
  "edges": [
    { "id": "/points.out.layer->/pixel-outline.par.layer", "source": "/points", "sourceHandle": "out.layer", "target": "/pixel-outline", "targetHandle": "par.layer" }
  ]
}
```

Connect `/pixel-outline`'s `out.layer` to `layers` on a [DeckRenderer](./deck-renderer.md) in place of the layer itself.
